items.stem: Mateo's prompt turns support tickets into bug titles. All three examples are about login errors, and now most titles mention login. What should he change first?

options.text: Replace two examples with tickets about other features, keeping the same title format.
options.feedback: Right. The examples share a topic the real inputs do not, so the model copies it. Vary the inputs, keep the format.

options.text: Add an instruction telling the model not to mention login unless needed.
options.feedback: Instructions help, but the examples still teach 'login' more strongly than one sentence can undo. Fix the examples first.

options.text: Remove the examples so the model is not biased by them.
options.feedback: Without examples the format becomes inconsistent. The problem is the narrow set, not having examples.

items.rationale: Targets the misconception that instructions override example bias.

items.stem: Ama compares two prompts. Prompt A has three examples in slightly different formats. Prompt B has three examples in an identical format, wrapped in <example> tags. Outputs from A vary in structure; outputs from B do not. What best explains the difference?

options.text: Prompt B's examples are longer, so the model pays more attention to them.
options.feedback: Length is not the difference here. Both prompts have three examples.

options.text: The model copies the format the examples share; in A they share no single format.
options.feedback: Correct. Examples teach format strongly. Consistent formats and clear tags give consistent outputs.

options.text: XML tags make the model follow instructions more strictly in general.
options.feedback: Tags help the model tell examples apart from instructions, but the consistent format is what fixed the output.

items.rationale: Separates the effect of tags from the effect of a consistent format.
